pages.title: Start in minutes
pages.description: Try TgWitness with sample data, then launch your own Telegram observation workspace on Windows, Linux or macOS.
pages.keywords: demo install setup windows linux macos python
pages.text: First, explore a working example. Then connect your own account. Look around without an account Download or clone the project, install Python 3.11 or later , and run the demo. The launcher creates a local environment and installs the pinned dependencies. git clone https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness.git cd TgWitness Windows .\scripts\Demo.cmd Linux / macOS sh start.sh --demo The browser opens a workspace with fictional messages. Open a conversation, compare an edit and inspect an export. Demo mode does not connect to Telegram. A sample workspace. Your own journal starts separately. Start your own workspace Close the demo process, then use the normal launcher: Windows .\Start.cmd Linux / macOS sh start.sh Open the local address shown by the launcher. If asked, enter the panel access token from the local file named in the terminal. This unlocks TgWitness; it is separate from Telegram sign-in. Capture your first message Connect a dedicated Telegram account. Select a group or channel the account can access, then start observation. Send a new message in a test group you control and check that it appears in the journal. For a server installation, follow Keep it running .

pages.title: Connect an account
pages.description: Connect Telegram by QR code, phone number or session import. Choose sources and check that new messages reach your journal.
pages.keywords: qr phone session tdata api id hash account sources
pages.text: One workspace holds one account, its journal and its signing key. Choose how to sign in Open Accounts , add a workspace and open its connection settings. Use a dedicated account for observation. QR code: scan it from Telegram’s device settings and confirm the new login. Phone number: enter the number, the code Telegram sends and your two-step verification password if enabled. Session import: import a supported session or Telegram Desktop data belonging to you. Choose a built-in API profile or enter your own API ID and hash. An API profile identifies the client; it does not sign in to an account or make the connection anonymous. Need a proxy first? You can choose and test the connection route before signing in. Each account has its own route. Choose what to observe Open the source list and select the chats, groups or channels you need. Review collection settings, including media, before starting observation. Start the collector and check its connection and recent activity. The account must be able to access the source. Different roles can see different events; the journal reflects what that account received. For a case spanning the entire account, use Sources → Observation scope → Investigation mode , review the settings and press Save scope . The complete investigation walkthrough covers all visible chat types, old history, people profiles, cross-chat references and evidence handoff. Check the whole path In a test group you control, send a unique message from another account, edit it and delete it. Confirm all three events in the journal, then export and verify the record. A connected status confirms the connection. A captured test message confirms that a particular event reached this workspace. Add another account Create another workspace in Accounts and repeat the setup. Keep each account’s signing-key fingerprint so you can identify its exports later.

pages.title: Choose a proxy
pages.description: Maintain automatic MTProxy routes or use your own proxy. Choose IP modes, fallback rules and the route for external requests.
pages.keywords: mtproto mtproxy socks5 http automatic pool IP modes fallback network public lists
pages.text: Keep the account connected. Decide explicitly when its route may use the server's address. Choose the IP mode first 01 Hide IP Use a proxy. When none works, wait without a direct Telegram connection. 02 Allow fallback Permit Direct after the configured delay; return to a working proxy when one answers. 03 Tunnel / VPN Allow direct routes through the host's network. This option does not install or verify a VPN. The route chooses the connection. The IP mode determines whether a direct connection is permitted. Let the pool maintain the route Open Account → Settings → Connection settings . Choose the IP mode and Automatic MTProxy , or enter a fixed route. Save and run Test Telegram connection . It also works before sign-in. After starting collection, check that a controlled message reaches the journal. New workspaces use automatic MTProxy with Hide IP behavior. The pool combines four public sources, probes entries, retains working routes and replaces failing proxies. Failed downloads retain the previous snapshots. Use your own proxy Enter SOCKS5 or HTTP CONNECT details, paste a supported Telegram proxy link, or provide an operator catalog. Pause observation before changing an active route. Fake TLS MTProxy secrets beginning with ee remain unsupported. Rotation, sharing and retry settings Under Parameters → Automatic MTProxy , set failure thresholds, cooldowns, planned rotation and accounts per proxy. A sharing limit of one makes an account wait when no exclusive entry is available. List refresh and probe intervals follow the main workspace's values. Separate proxies do not guarantee separate exit IPs. Separate Telegram from external requests MTProxy carries Telegram traffic only. Timestamps, notifications, copies and source checks use a separate SOCKS5/HTTP proxy, the account's SOCKS5/HTTP route, or Direct where the IP mode permits it. Those external requests can be disabled. An explicit TGWITNESS_PROXY_FEED_PROXY configures the feed downloader's route. The independent witness keeps its own settings. These controls do not install a system VPN or route browser traffic. See all modes, defaults and source lists , or choose who may change an account's route .

pages.title: Export and verify
pages.description: Export captured Telegram history, verify signatures and compare a journal with a checkpoint retained by an independent witness.
pages.keywords: evidence signature hash integrity verify zip fingerprint checkpoint s3 backup restore recovery object lock
pages.text: Share a signed record that someone else can check. Retain a reference Export signed ZIP Recipient verifies New to signatures and checkpoints? Change a sample record and see which checks detect it. Keeping a copy away from the collector? Go to S3 setup , Object Lock or verified recovery . Retain a trusted reference Save the workspace’s public-key fingerprint outside the collector. During collection, keep signed checkpoints elsewhere or use an independent witness . These references let a recipient check the key and an earlier journal boundary. Download the signed ZIP Open Exports and create a signed evidence ZIP. It includes the workspace journal and a signed file manifest. Panel filters do not limit this full-journal export: review the material before sharing it. Standalone HTML and CSV downloads are useful for reading and analysis. Keep the signed ZIP as the verifiable original; the separate HTML or CSV file has no standalone signature. Verify with a trusted copy of TgWitness In the installed project environment, replace the example fingerprint and file paths: python -m tgwitness.verify evidence.zip --fingerprint TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256 --checkpoint retained-checkpoint.json When both references pass, the result reports key_pinned: true and checkpoint_checked: true . Keep the verification result with the original archive. The retained checkpoint must be at or before the export’s boundary. Understand the result Integrity: the recorded history and exported files match their signatures. Earlier observation: an external checkpoint lets you compare the export with a previously retained journal prefix. Delivery: a controlled send → edit → delete test checks specific events against the captured record. A valid signature does not prove that every Telegram event arrived, that the source told the truth or that the collector’s clock was correct. Set up the S3 off-site copy In your running workspace, open Exports → Off-site copy . This optional feature works with AWS S3 and other S3-compatible services. It copies journal segments, preserved photos and files, checkpoints with their timestamp responses, and finished chat exports. Every object is encrypted on the collector with AES-256-GCM before upload. The online demo shows the same controls with uploads disabled. Enter storage credentials only in your own running workspace. The complete panel with advanced options expanded. No storage credentials are shown. Storage settings in Exports → Off-site copy Field What to enter Endpoint The storage service URL, without a bucket path or credentials. Fictional example: https://s3.example.invalid . Region The region required by your provider. The application default is us-east-1 . Bucket An existing bucket you can access. Fictional example: example-case-backup . Folder in the bucket The object prefix; default tgwitness . The application appends a prefix derived from this workspace’s signing-key fingerprint. Access key ID / Secret access key Enter both storage credentials together. They are saved in the workspace vault. Leave both empty on later saves to keep the saved pair. Path-style addresses Use endpoint/bucket when enabled, or bucket.endpoint when disabled, according to the provider. Copy interval From 1 to 1,440 minutes; default 5 minutes. The application must be running for scheduled copies. Object Lock retention Retention days and mode for a bucket that supports Object Lock. Zero days leaves the bucket’s default retention in effect. Enter the destination and credentials. Leave Keep an off-site copy unchecked while preparing, then select Save off-site copy . Select Test connection . This uploads an encrypted test object and checks the storage response. Select Download encryption key . Keep that file separately from the collector; it is required for recovery. Enable the Keep an off-site copy checkbox and save again. Select Copy now for a manual pass, or leave the schedule running. Does not do It does not create a storage bucket. Scheduled uplo

pages.title: See how evidence works
pages.description: Follow a message from capture to checkpoint. Change a sample record, recalculate its SHA-256 chain and see what a retained checkpoint detects.
pages.keywords: visual animation diagram formula sha256 hash chain canonical signature tamper learn
pages.text: A message can change. The record of what you observed should remain checkable. Explore two small experiments below. They use fictional messages, stay in your browser and never connect to Telegram. One message, three observations When Telegram delivers a new message, an edit and a deletion notice, the collector appends three separate observations. The edit does not replace the first record. A deletion notice does not erase it. 01 / MESSAGE JOURNEY Illustrative sequence CURRENT CHAT VIEW Message #42 Message deleted The message has disappeared from the chat view. OBSERVATION JOURNAL 3 records 01 message.new Meet at 10:00 ✓ 02 message.edited Meet at 11:00 ✓ 03 message.deleted Deletion notice for #42 ✓ Play sequence Next event → Reset Ready / 0 of 3 All three received observations remain in the journal. Simplified path for one already selected source. Operational records also share the real journal. Capture depends on what the account can see and what Telegram delivers. A deletion notice supplies neither a reliable deletion time nor the person who deleted the message. Keeping those values unknown preserves the distinction between an observation and a guess. Change a record. Follow the hash. Each record contains the previous record’s hash. Its own hash covers the event fields, including that link. An externally retained checkpoint pins a specific journal length and head hash. 02 / HASH-CHAIN SANDBOX Real SHA-256 · sample records Original Alter record 2 Rebuild its hashes Remove the tail RECORD 01 Message received h₁ = SHA-256(e₁) Links to 64 zeroes RECORD 02 Meet at 11:00 h₂ = SHA-256(e₂) Includes h₁ RECORD 03 Deletion observed h₃ = SHA-256(e₃) Includes h₂ RETAINED ELSEWHERE 3 records · head h₃ Compare this fixed boundary with the supplied journal. Altering an event changes its hash. Rebuilding the chain changes its head. Removing the tail makes it shorter than the retained checkpoint. Inspect record 2 and the full hashes This is the exact UTF-8 JSON hashed in this example. Values are fictional; the nine fields and serialization match the journal format. Saved record 2 hash Recalculated record 2 hash This sandbox computes hashes, not signatures. The real verifier also checks every event’s Ed25519 signature, sequence and link. Rebuilding hashes alone cannot create valid signatures under the trusted key. The actual rules, in a few lines HASH + SIGNATURE h 0 = 0 64 h i = hex(SHA-256(C(e i ))) σ i = Ed25519.Sign(sk, unhex(h i )) C serializes the nine event fields as UTF-8 JSON: sorted keys, no extra whitespace, no ASCII escaping and no NaN/infinity. The event’s previous_hash is h i−1 . The displayed h 0 means 64 zero characters; signatures cover the 32 raw digest bytes. The nine fields are seq , observed_at , source_at , kind , chat_id , message_id , actor_id , payload and previous_hash . This is TgWitness’s documented JSON encoding ; the hash and signature themselves are not hash-input fields. RETAINED CHECKPOINT N export ≥ N checkpoint h export [N checkpoint ] = H checkpoint Verify the checkpoint signature under the pinned collector key, then compare its boundary with the verified journal. A later export may contain more records; it must still agree at the earlier checkpoint. Three questions, three different checks 01 / INTEGRITY Did this record change? Verify hashes and signatures against a separately trusted key. 02 / CONTINUITY What was retained earlier? Compare a signed export with checkpoints kept by a separate witness. 03 / DELIVERY Did these test events arrive? Match controlled send, edit and delete actions against each account’s journal. A matching hash chain answers an integrity question. It does not establish complete Telegram delivery, the truth of a message or an independently trusted observation time. Follow the whole-account investigation from acquisition to case package.

pages.title: Investigate across all chats
pages.description: Run an end-to-end Telegram investigation across channels, groups, private chats and bots: whole-account capture, history, people, links, files, timelines and verified evidence.
pages.keywords: use cases scenarios investigation all chats whole account history dossier people links files timeline case package
pages.text: Work an entire case across channels, groups, private chats and bots: collect, connect, reconstruct and hand over the evidence. This walkthrough follows one fictional incident through a whole account. It uses the actual collection, search, people-profile and export features. The case map is a documentation example; your conclusions and case register are maintained outside the application. WORKED CASE / A CHANGED PAYMENT DESTINATION One incident. Four conversations. A trail to reconstruct. A channel announcement points to a bot. An operations group discusses a new payment link. A private follow-up repeats it. Later, the announcement is edited and a group message disappears. Who posted each version? Where did the link appear? Which file was preserved? What changed, and when? 1. All chats 2. History & files 3. Live actions 4. Connections 5. Timeline 6. Other accounts 7. Case package More investigations 1. Establish coverage across the whole account Connect the collecting account in its own workspace. Record the case reference, account ID, workspace name and signing-key fingerprint in your case notes. Open Sources → Observation scope → Investigation mode . Review Whole account , all four source types and Own actions . This preset enables saving a new source’s profile and its latest 200 visible messages . Press Save scope and complete the scope confirmation. Press Load chats . Compare the sources with the account’s dialog list and review exclusions. Under Parameters → Chats read from the account’s list , adjust the initial list limit if needed: the default is 1,000 dialogs, configurable up to 20,000. Chats beyond the limit are discovered when they become active. In Recording settings , select and save All visible activity . Review attachment types, size limits and free disk space. Start observation and validate a controlled message, edit and deletion before relying on the setup. Channels Groups Private chats Bots ONE ACCOUNT / ONE SIGNING KEY All selected account-visible activity → one journal Messages · edits · deletion notices · visible reactions · membership events · own actions “Whole account” covers the chats this account can access, with the configured source types and exclusions. Secret chats are unavailable. New dialogs are added as updates arrive; enabling this mode does not automatically download the complete old history of every existing chat. 2. Acquire history and preserve the files Build a source register for the entire investigation. Give every chat a row with its numeric ID, title, account, access/role, live start, history acquisition, media result and known gaps. Mark a source as acquired only after checking the relevant result. Choose the acquisition that answers the question Need Action in the panel What it provides Existing chat context in the journal Sources → Recording settings → History snapshot Recent visible messages as signed observations. Default maximum 500; Parameters → Largest history snapshot can raise it up to 10,000. Complete currently visible history of one chat Full chat export → Export full chat, or Chats → Export chat A separate signed bundle with chat.json and chat.html . Repeat per source; retain completion/failure results. Context when a new chat appears Observation scope → When a new chat or bot appears A source profile and up to 1,000 recent visible messages; Investigation mode selects 200. Existing chats do not receive this intake retroactively. Attachment bytes Download visible attachments + per-type limits Check for media.saved , its SHA-256 and byte count. A queued, skipped or failed download is not a preserved file. A full chat export is a separate snapshot; it does not import its entire history into the journal or people profiles. Use journal snapshots for the historical material you need to search and analyze inside TgWitness. Full history acquisition currently runs per chat; there is no single action that backfills every chat in an account. In the worked case, acquire the announcemen

pages.title: Keep it secure
pages.description: See where sessions, keys and evidence live, what leaves your machine, what the protections cover and how to harden an installation.
pages.keywords: security threat model secrets vault token encryption hardening privacy vulnerability report
pages.text: Know the routes for Telegram, public proxy lists and optional external services. Know what each secret unlocks, what the protections cover and what they leave to you. 127.0.0.1 panel address by default 256-bit random panel token 0 CDNs, analytics or remote fonts Ed25519 signature on every record Where everything lives The collector, its panel and every saved record stay on the computer or server you run it on. Telegram is the only destination by default; each other one is a separate switch. 06 / WHAT LEAVES THE MACHINE Your installation Off-site copy Notifications Timestamps Witness YOUR COMPUTER OR SERVER Panel 127.0.0.1:8787 · bearer token Collector one Telegram client per workspace DATA DIRECTORY Journal SQLite · hash-chained · signed Media files named by SHA-256 Vault Fernet · session, API pair, signing key, proxy Telegram Always · through your route The account's MTProto connection: direct, SOCKS5, HTTP or MTProxy. Hide IP mode waits for a working proxy. Direct fallback requires a mode that explicitly permits it. Off-site copy Optional · off by default Journal, files and checkpoints encrypted with AES-GCM before upload to S3-compatible storage. The key stays with you; attachments are named by keyed hashes, not their content hash. Notifications Optional · off by default Problems and change counts with chat titles. Message excerpts are sent only if you turn them on. Timestamp authority Optional · off by default Only the SHA-256 of a signed checkpoint and a random nonce. No messages, no chat names. Witness Optional · off by default Pulls signed checkpoints and capture counters with a read-only token. It cannot read conversations or change settings. Default: only the Telegram connection leaves this machine. Optional destinations are configured per workspace. Message text and media are stored unencrypted in the data directory: protect it with disk encryption and file permissions. What each secret unlocks Secret Where it is kept What it unlocks If it leaks Panel token panel-token.txt in the data directory; the browser keeps it for the tab only Everything in every workspace: read and export, change scope, sign in accounts Stop TgWitness, delete panel-token.txt , start it again: a new token is created Telegram session Vault, encrypted ( credentials.enc ) The Telegram account itself End the session in Telegram under Settings → Devices Signing key Vault, encrypted ( signing.enc ) Signing records that verify under your fingerprint Checkpoints kept elsewhere, a witness and timestamps show what existed before Vault key vault.key beside the data, or an external master key for a new data directory Decrypting the vault Treat the session and signing key as leaked too Witness token On the witness host Read-only: signed checkpoints and health Delete it on the Witness page; create a new one Off-site copy key Vault; download it once for recovery Decrypting the off-site copy Whoever also holds the stored objects can decrypt them: treat that copy as exposed What the protections cover ✓ Covered A changed, removed or reordered record in an export: the hash chain or a signature no longer verifies. A journal cut back or rebuilt after a checkpoint was kept elsewhere: the retained checkpoint no longer matches. Guessing the panel token: 256 random bits, compared in constant time; after 15 failures a minute an address is refused. Hostile chat content: text is inserted as text, never as HTML; attachments download as files; the panel loads nothing from other sites. A copied data directory with an external vault key: sessions and signing keys stay encrypted without the master key. ! Left to you The main panel token has full control. Give other people scoped access to the accounts, chats and actions they need; keep the main key private. An administrator of the machine can read everything and rewrite and re-sign the journal. Keep the fingerprint and checkpoints on another system. Message text and media are not encrypted by TgWitness. Use disk encryption and

pages.title: Share a case
pages.description: Give reviewers and analysts access to selected accounts and chats, with separate permissions, session limits and revocable tokens.
pages.keywords: access permissions roles scope reviewer analyst token sessions IP expiry revoke
pages.text: Share the case someone needs. Keep control of the rest. 01 Choose the evidence Select whole account workspaces or individual recorded chats. 02 Choose the actions Allow viewing, export or the specific operational permissions the person needs. 03 Set the limits Issue a personal token with an expiry, session limits and optional IP restrictions. Collection scope decides what is recorded. Access scope decides what a person can see and do. Give someone access Sign in as the administrator and open Access . Name the access and select workspaces and chats. Keep View for a reviewer. Add Export if they should download records. Set limits, then press Create access . Copy the token shown once. Send it privately with the panel address. Check the allowed view in a separate browser session before handing it over. Start with the job they need to do Person Access Result Reviewer Selected chats; view only Read the captured conversation without changing collection. Analyst Selected chats; view and export Review and download the records needed for the case. Operator Selected whole workspaces; sources and collection Manage what is observed and start or stop collectors. These are configurations you choose, not fixed roles. Account-wide settings and full journal exports stay closed to chat-limited access even when another permission is enabled. All-workspace access includes future accounts. Change your mind at any time Edit the access to change what subsequent requests can do. End one session or revoke the whole access to end all its sessions. Files already downloaded cannot be recalled. Ending a panel session does not stop collection. Session and IP limits Limit parallel sessions and successful sign-ins, set an absolute end date, allow IP addresses or subnets, or bind access to its first sign-in address. Session expiry measures inactivity; an open panel's polling counts as activity. Check the client address shown by the application when it runs behind a proxy or tunnel. The main key and the activity log The administrator keeps the main panel token. Issued access cannot manage other people's access or open the administrator console. The console shows current-process activity across workspaces; signed access records retain grant and session events without tokens. Workspaces share the host process and do not isolate data from the server administrator. Use the full permission reference for all seven permissions, session rules and the administrator boundary.

pages.title: Set up a witness bot
pages.description: Publish signed journal checkpoints to your Telegram channel with a separate witness, its own key and read-only collector access.
pages.keywords: bot botfather telegram channel continuity checkpoint independent witness
pages.text: Let a separate process check the journal and publish signed checkpoints to your channel. Two hosts, two signing keys HOST A / COLLECTOR Account + journal Telegram session Collector signing key Read-only checkpoint endpoint ← request signed answer → HOST B / WITNESS Verify + retain Pinned collector fingerprint Separate witness signing key Own journal + bot token Witness → Telegram Bot API → Your channel · signed TGW1 posts The witness pulls checks itself. Collector access is read-only. Bot publication uses the witness’s connection and token; no account session is given to the witness. 03 / CHECKPOINT DECISIONS Illustrative answers Journal grows Count goes back Same count, new head No response LAST ACCEPTED 120 records head 9c7d… → NEXT ANSWER 128 records head a4f2… Accepted: the count grows, the signature verifies and the key matches. The witness retains this new boundary. All answering examples assume a valid signature and the pinned key. Hashes here are abbreviated illustrations. A larger count alone cannot prove that the entire old prefix is unchanged; compare an export with retained checkpoints. Prepare a bot and a channel Create a bot with BotFather and allow it to post in a channel you control. Choose a computer or server for the witness. A separate host and operator provide stronger independence than a second process on the collector’s server. Three steps in Extras Read-only access. Open Extras → A bot in your channel , create a witness token and save the access file. It allows reading checkpoints and health, not conversations or collector controls. Channel and interval. Enter the channel and a collector address reachable from the witness. Save the settings file. Launch. Put witness.json , witness-token.txt and a bot-token.txt created on the witness host together. Run the commands below in the installed project environment. python -m tgwitness.witness run --config witness.json --check-config python -m tgwitness.witness run --config witness.json Downloading the files does not start the witness. Check that the first signed post appears in the channel, then retain the witness’s public-key fingerprint separately. Choose how often to publish Publishing every check creates a regular external record. At five-minute intervals, that is about 288 posts per workspace per day. The advanced settings also offer publication on changes or problems, a proxy and a custom Bot API address. What does the bot actually attest to? The witness asks the collector for a signed checkpoint, verifies it against the expected key and keeps a separate signed journal. It records missing responses and rejected answers as well as successful checks. Publication still depends on the witness running and reaching Telegram’s Bot API. It checks the collector’s reported journal state. It does not independently observe every Telegram message. For that, add the controlled delivery test. Check the evidence later Keep the witness journal, channel posts and independently saved fingerprints. The full verification procedure compares them with the collector’s signed export.

pages.title: Keep it running
pages.description: Run TgWitness on a server with persistent storage, private panel access, backups and checks after a restart.
pages.keywords: docker compose deployment vps backup restore update restart operations
pages.text: Keep the collector available and its data intact across restarts. Choose a launch method For a native installation, use the launcher and the service examples in deploy/ . For Docker, install Docker with Compose and run from the project directory: docker compose up -d --build --wait docker compose exec tgwitness cat /data/panel-token.txt The default panel listens on the host’s loopback address, port 8787. Open it locally or through an SSH tunnel. Use the token from the second command to unlock the panel. Keep the whole data directory Native installations use data/live . Docker uses the persistent tgwitness-data volume. Keep journals, account sessions, keys and operational state together. A signed export is useful evidence, but it is not a full installation backup. Stop collection before taking a consistent backup. Copy the full private data directory to protected storage outside the host. Test restoration into an isolated installation before relying on the backup. Check after a restart Confirm the expected workspace and key, Telegram connection, selected sources and new message capture. Saved MTProto state and catch-up help recover updates that Telegram still retains. They cannot reconstruct every expired update or an edit deleted before capture. Container health means the web server responds. Use a controlled message and a witness check to assess collection and external publication. Publish only what you intend The deployment reference includes HTTPS examples, persistent-volume commands, updates and restore steps. Docker commands are provided for deployment; the current validation record identifies the environments actually tested.

pages.title: Find what went wrong
pages.description: Check panel access, Telegram connection, missing messages, FloodWait and witness status using the right signals for each problem.
pages.keywords: help error token login disconnected floodwait gap pts qts recovery github
pages.text: Start with the symptom. Check one layer at a time. The panel asks for a token Use the panel token from the local file shown by the launcher. For Docker, run docker compose exec tgwitness cat /data/panel-token.txt . A Telegram login code, BotFather token and read-only witness token serve different purposes. Telegram does not connect Open connection settings and run the connection check. If using a public proxy, try another entry and save the route explicitly. Check the proxy type and supported secret format. Refreshing a public list does not switch the account’s route. Connected, but no new messages Check that observation is running in the right workspace. Confirm the source is selected and visible to that account. Send a unique new message in a controlled group and look for that exact text. Review the operational journal for interruptions, delayed work or Telegram errors. Historical snapshots and new-message events are different. A quiet source can be connected without producing new messages. Use a controlled delivery test when completeness matters. FloodWait or a gap after a restart FloodWait means Telegram requires a pause. Wait for the indicated period and review collection workload; repeated reconnects do not remove the limit. Saved update state helps catch up after a restart, but expired updates and some interruption windows remain limitations. Record the gap rather than treating the journal as complete. The bot is configured but posts nothing Make sure the witness process is actually running, the bot can post in the channel and the witness can reach the collector and Bot API. Inspect its journal for failed publications. A successful collector poll alone does not confirm a channel post. Where is GitHub token integration? Planned. Extras describes the proposed fork and build verification workflow. There is currently no GitHub token form or automated attestation that a running installation matches a repository. See the current feature status . When reporting a problem, include the version, operating system, steps and a redacted error. Keep sessions, tokens, private messages and the data directory out of public issues.

pages.title: Modes, scenarios and evidence levels
pages.description: Collection scopes, event boundaries, eight verification mechanisms and six fictional investigation scenarios.
pages.keywords: One journal. Four collection modes. Eight verification levels.
pages.text: Modes, scenarios and evidence levels | TgWitness Skip to content TgWitness v0.7.0 Setup guide Dedicated account Back to panel English English Русский Українська Español Português (Brasil) Türkçe العربية فارسی اردو हिन्दी Bahasa Indonesia Tiếng Việt 简体中文 Français Deutsch Italiano O‘zbekcha 한국어 繁體中文 Bahasa Melayu Polski 日本語 ไทย עברית বাংলা አማርኛ Modes, scenarios and evidence levels One journal. Four collection modes. Eight verification levels. TgWitness records what the connected account observes. A third party can verify the record’s integrity against an independently trusted key. Collection modes ↘ Scenarios ↘ Evidence levels ↘ 3–5 minute overview · fictional examples · current implementation 01 Telegram Account-visible updates 02 Collector Linked records, each signed 03 Verifier Trusted key + retained boundary h₁ → h₂ → h₃ · Ed25519 Integrity is checked. Telegram origin and the truth of a message remain separate questions. 01 Choose the observation scope Three scopes and an investigation preset. Exclusions and enabled source types still apply. Default Chosen chats Records Only sources selected by hand. New chats Not added automatically. Choose for A known set of channels or groups. No fixed chat capacity has been qualified. pages.text: TgWitness signs in as a Telegram user account (not a bot) over MTProto, using Telethon. Each account lives in its own workspace (called a workspace in the API and command-line tools) with its own session, sources, journal and signing key. Session files, session strings and Auth Keys are account authorizations : whoever holds one can act as that account. They do not contain message history. [!WARNING] Do not use anything you cannot afford to lose. We strongly advise against connecting personal or otherwise valuable accounts, and against creating an API ID / API hash on an account you value. This is not about TgWitness being untested: Telegram restricts and permanently bans accounts unpredictably — for request volumes it happens to consider excessive, regardless of the client or purpose, with no adequate documentation. Many bans are irreversible. Use dedicated accounts. Smooth test runs depend on Telegram, not on the software, and guarantee nothing for later. At a glance Before you start: API ID and API hash Phone number · QR code · Auth Key + DC ID Account files : Telethon .session · Pyrogram .session · Session + JSON pair · TData · StringSession · Account JSON Identify what you have · Unsupported formats Multiple accounts · Keeping account files safe · Troubleshooting At a glance # What you have Tab in Add account You will also need The phone number and access to its login codes Phone 2FA password if enabled Telegram open on another device QR code 2FA password if enabled A .session file (Telethon or Pyrogram) Files Optional companion JSON for app settings .session + .json with the same name Files (select both) Usually nothing else A Telegram Desktop tdata folder Files (as a ZIP) The Desktop local passcode if one is set A Telethon StringSession (text, .txt , .tgwitness-session ) Files No separate API pair required A .json with a session or Auth Key Files No separate API pair required An Auth Key (512 hex characters) and its DC number Auth key Optional User ID TgWitness recognises files by their contents , not their names. Renaming a file never converts it. Before you start: API ID and API hash # You can sign in without creating a Telegram API application. When no pair is entered, imported or already saved in the workspace, TgWitness picks a pair from its built-in pool of 50 public API pairs ( tgwitness/api_pool.py ) in random order. If Telegram refuses a pair ( API_ID_INVALID , API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD , UPDATE_APP_TO_LOGIN ), the next one is tried, up to eight per sign-in; refused pairs are skipped until restart. The pair that signed in is saved with the account and reused for it. An API ID and API hash identify the application to Telegram; they do not authorize an account by themselves. To use your own application instead (the account that registers it is the one at risk; see Why a built-in API pool? ): Open my.telegram.org and sign in with any phone number you own. The code arrives in the Telegram app, not by SMS. Choose API development tools . Create an application: any title and short name (5–32 letters), platform Desktop . URL and description can stay empty. Copy App api_id (a number) and App api_hash (32 hexadecimal characters). In the panel, open API ID + Hash under the sign-in form. You can paste a single api_id:api_hash pair into API ID and both fields are filled. One pair can be used for all of your accounts. After a successful login it is saved, encrypted, in that workspace only and is never sent back to the browser. Precedence: a pair entered in the form, then one from an imported account JSON, then the pair saved in the workspace, then the built-in pool of 50 public pairs, tried in random order with automatic rotation when Telegram refuses one. Only the Telegram Desktop pair (2040) is sent with a matching Telegram Desktop client description. pages.text: TgWitness records what a connected Telegram account observes. The journal preserves those observations, their sequence, and the context supplied with them. It does not infer unseen actions from a missing message or from an account being connected. From login to a journal # Diagram as text Authorize a user account → Select accessible groups and channels Select accessible groups and channels → Save event and attachment settings Save event and attachment settings → Start observation Start observation → Receive updates from the active client Receive updates from the active client → Apply source and event policy Apply source and event policy → Append a signed observation Append a signed observation → Review or export the journal Append a signed observation → Process any queued attachment Process any queued attachment → Append the download outcome Authorization, access to a source, a running collector, and complete delivery are different questions. A successful login does not grant access to every group. A connected transport does not establish that every relevant update arrived. Observation scope: chosen chats, a folder or the whole account # Sources → Observation scope decides which chats a workspace records. Mode Records New chats Chosen chats (default) Only the chats you add by hand Never added automatically Telegram folder Chats in one of the account's folders: chats included by name, plus the folder's categories (contacts, non-contacts, groups, channels, bots), minus its excluded chats and, if the folder says so, archived chats Matching chats are added as soon as they become active; chats you add to the folder in Telegram are picked up within an hour Whole account Every chat the account sees Every new chat, group, private chat or bot is added the moment its first update arrives Source types (channels, groups, private chats, bots) narrow the folder and whole-account modes. Chosen chats can be of any type, including private chats and bots. Excluded chats are never recorded, in any mode. In folder and whole-account modes, Exclude and Remove on a source put it on this list, so the scope does not add it again. Choosing the chat again by hand (in Sources or from Chats) takes it off the list. The list holds up to 5,000 chats; past that, Remove is refused and the chat can be paused instead. Own actions (on by default): messages this account sends, its edits and its reply-keyboard button presses. Turned off, outgoing messages and edits are skipped. Switching to a folder or the whole account asks for confirmation: these modes record private chats and messages of third parties and belong on a dedicated account only. The confirmation and every scope change are signed scope.changed records. Chats added by the scope appear as sources marked auto , recorded as scope.applied (at start and hourly) or source.discovered (a new chat while observing). Switching back to chosen chats pauses every automatically added source. What these modes cannot do: Secret chats are end-to-end encrypted between two devices and never reach TgWitness, in any mode. Nothing is recorded while TgWitness is not running. After a restart it asks Telegram for missed updates and rechecks chats, but Telegram does not return everything after long outages. Reports and verify.py show such periods as gaps (see coverage ). Only the first 1,000 dialogs are listed at start (the limit is under Parameters ); older chats are added when they next become active. The earlier history of an added chat is not fetched — take a history snapshot or a full chat export when you need it. Folder conditions that change all the time (muted, read) are not applied: such chats stay observed. Inline (callback) bot buttons pressed in another app are invisible to a second session; the bot's reply or edit is recorded. pages.text: Follow a case across channels, groups, private chats and bots, from initial acquisition to a cited timeline and verifiable handoff. The interactive website version is at /docs/cases/ ; preview instructions . Worked case: a destination changes across four conversations # An announcement points to a bot. An operations group discusses a new payment destination, the bot's keyboard displays it, and a private follow-up repeats it. The announcement is then edited and a group message disappears. pages.text: Design reference: 26 October 2026. The primary use case is private Telegram groups and channels accessible to the connected accounts. This document separates implemented behavior, platform boundaries and future work. A target architecture item is not a claim that the feature already exists. Standalone application # TgWitness has its own installation, data directory, and release lifecycle. The bundled web interface handles setup and review; exported records can be used independently. The operator connects their accounts, chooses sources visible to each, and obtains a saved observation journal. The panel exposes content, saved changes, observation provenance and known gaps. Another investigator can verify the exported material. Four distinct states matter: account authorization, access to a source, a working collector, and the extent to which delivery completeness is established. None of the first three automatically proves the fourth. A quiet group is not necessarily a failed collector. Shared investigations # An administrator can issue access tokens scoped to workspaces and individual chats, with seven permissions, IP restrictions, expiry, sign-in limits and session control. A read-only reviewer can inspect a case without receiving Telegram authorization or the main panel key. Chat-limited access stays separate from account-wide settings and full-journal exports. Automatic MTProxy maintains working Telegram routes from four public sources or an operator catalog. IP modes determine whether failure must wait for another proxy or may use an explicitly permitted direct route. External HTTP requests have a separate route and off switch. Optional extras # Everyday setup is account → sources → observation. Extras is a separate destination with two cards: a Telegram witness bot and planned GitHub build verification. Each states its availability and requirements before showing settings. Choosing a card opens instructions; it does not enroll or start a service. Bot setup has three steps: create read-only access, choose publication settings, and launch on the witness host. Network and publication options, existing connections and verification commands are disclosed on demand. Downloaded configuration is distinct from a running witness. Switching extras retains the draft; account changes and locking clear the temporary token and form. The built-in guide includes launch instructions. GitHub remains a marked plan, with no credential form or pretend connection state. Protocol and private sources # MTProto is Telegram's protocol; Telethon is the Python library TgWitness uses to speak MTProto. They are not alternative connection methods. Collection uses MTProto; the optional witness publishes signed checks through the Bot API. Each workspace has its own authorized client and account update stream. TgWitness selects observations from configured sources and makes separate explicit requests for functions such as history snapshots and media downloads. A private source needs no public username. Telegram peer type and numeric ID are the identifiers; titles and usernames can change. Access depends on existing membership and permissions. TgWitness does not automatically join sources or bypass join approval. An access hash from another account is not a universal access token. The collection model must account for pre-join hidden history, participant/admin roles, session revocation, removal or changed permissions, group-to-supergroup migration, topics/forums, linked discussions, channel identities and unavailable attachments. Not every combination has been qualified live. Source visibility is checked at collector start. Missing a source from the bounded dialog result means access unconfirmed , not proven removal. pages.description: Hash chain, signatures, checkpoints and witnesses explained with the exact formulas the verifier uses.
pages.keywords: hash chain sha256 ed25519 canonical json checkpoint formula
pages.text: TgWitness preserves what a collecting account observed, links those observations into a signed journal and lets another person verify an export against a trusted key and an earlier retained checkpoint. The local documentation website adds interactive examples at /docs/concepts/ , a checkpoint decision explorer at /docs/witness/ . All example messages, counts and delays are fictional. Hashes in the chain sandbox are calculated with SHA-256 in the browser. Nothing is sent to Telegram. A message changes; observations accumulate # Diagram as text Telegram → Collector: New message: Meet at 10:00 Collector → Signed journal: Append message.new Telegram → Collector: Edit: Meet at 11:00 Collector → Signed journal: Append message.edited Telegram → Collector: Deletion notice Collector → Signed journal: Append message.deleted Note on Signed journal: Original + edit + deletion observation remain This simplified sequence assumes Telegram delivered each update and the selected account could see it. Operational events also share the journal. A deletion notice does not supply the deleter or an exact deletion time. Repeated deliveries are separate observations; there is no journal-wide duplicate suppression. What a hash covers # Read the formula from the inside out: C turns the nine fields into exact bytes; SHA-256 produces their digest; hex is how that digest is stored. The previous hash is already inside the event. unhex turns the stored hash back into the 32 bytes that Ed25519 signs. Static chain diagram Let C(e i ) be the canonical UTF-8 JSON of the nine event fields. The first previous_hash is 64 zero characters. Each later record includes the preceding record's hexadecimal hash: h i = hex(SHA256(C(e i ))) σ i = Ed25519.Sign(sk,unhex(h i )) The signature covers the 32 raw digest bytes. The hash input contains exactly seq , observed_at , source_at , kind , chat_id , message_id , actor_id , payload and previous_hash . Object keys are sorted; whitespace and ASCII escaping are omitted; NaN and infinity are rejected. See the exact encoding . Diagram as text 64 zero characters → Record 1 / hash h1 Record 1 / hash h1 → Record 2 includes h1 / hash h2 Record 2 includes h1 / hash h2 → Record 3 includes h2 / hash h3 Record 3 includes h2 / hash h3 → Signed checkpoint: count 3, head h3 (retain elsewhere) Change to the supplied journal What detects it Alter record 2 while leaving its saved hash Recomputed event hash differs; its signature no longer covers the changed event Rebuild the altered record and every later hash The original signatures fail; a retained checkpoint at the affected boundary also disagrees Remove the tail but keep the remaining prefix intact An earlier retained checkpoint beyond the supplied prefix reveals that the export is too short Re-sign a replacement journal with another key A separately trusted key fingerprint rejects the replacement identity Try the logic on record 2: change Meet at 11:00 to Meet at 12:00 in the saved event. Its recomputed hash no longer matches. Recalculating the later chain can repair its links, but cannot make the original signatures cover the new digests. An observed Telegram edit, by contrast, becomes a new journal record. Static change diagram Hash links alone do not prevent someone from recalculating a replacement chain. Trust comes from checking signatures under an independently trusted key and comparing with references retained outside the collector. What an earlier checkpoint adds # The reference stays still while the journal grows. If the checkpoint says “3 records, head h3”, a four-record export can pass by matching h3 at position 3. Its newest head is h4, which is expected to differ. An export of only two records fails. Static checkpoint diagram After verifying the checkpoint signature, require: N export ≥ N checkpoint and h export [N checkpoint ] = H checkpoint An export may extend beyond a checkpoint. It must agree at the retained boundary. The real verifier also checks every event's sequence,

pages.description: Contents of the signed ZIP, record kinds, process receipts, people profiles, off-site copies and offline verification.
pages.keywords: evidence zip manifest events jsonl verify dossier replica s3
pages.text: An observation is not a conclusion. A sender ID is not a real-world identity. The account-visible service update is the source; Telegram does not cryptographically sign these saved records for a third-party investigator. What is signed # Material Protection What to retain Every journal observation, including operational events SHA-256 chain and an Ed25519 signature per event Original events.jsonl , the trusted key fingerprint, and a retained checkpoint Evidence ZIP contents manifest.sig signs the canonical manifest, which lists hashes of the content files The complete ZIP, including its manifest and signature Preserved attachments SHA-256 and byte count in a signed media.saved event; file hash in the signed ZIP manifest The original bytes inside the verified ZIP Checkpoint Ed25519 signature over journal length, head hash, public key, and creation time An independent copy retained before a disputed change Run receipt Separately signed collector measurements; also included in a signed process.started event The receipt and associated journal; measurements are self-reported Standalone CSV or HTML No standalone cryptographic signature; event hashes alone are insufficient Use the exact copy inside the verified ZIP for integrity checking Screenshots, printouts, or PDF produced by a browser No TgWitness signature on the derivative Keep the original verified package and document how the derivative was made The collector verifies journal signatures before generating every export format. That source check does not create a signature on a separately downloaded CSV or HTML file. A valid JSONL event signature likewise does not provide the attachment bytes or independently establish that the entire observed journal was supplied. Investigation handoff # Record the case reference, operator, numeric Telegram account ID, selected sources, collection policy, and collection period in your case notes. TgWitness preserves observations; case assignment and custody records are managed outside the application. Qualify the intended collection setup with the live acceptance procedure . Retain the workspace's public-key fingerprint independently before relying on its exports. Save signed checkpoints outside the collector during collection. Record interruptions and the limits of the account's visibility. Export a signed ZIP and retain the signed run receipt. Use a checkpoint at or before the exported journal boundary. A later checkpoint can correctly reject an earlier export as too short. Exports include the full workspace journal, regardless of panel filters; review the material before sharing it. Have the recipient verify the ZIP with a trusted copy of the verifier and the independently supplied fingerprint/checkpoint. From a trusted checkout with its Python environment active: python -m tgwitness.verify evidence.zip --fingerprint TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256 --checkpoint retained-checkpoint.json Successful output reports key_pinned: true and checkpoint_checked: true when both inputs are supplied and accepted. Preserve the verification result. For a handover requiring the final exported record to be witnessed, use `--witness witness.zip --witness-fingerprint TRUSTED_WITNESS_SHA256 --require-witness`. This refuses an export with an unwitnessed tail. See the [witness handover procedure](WITNESS.md#require-a-witnessed-export-boundary). Record the archive's SHA-256, export boundary, transfer date, sender, and recipient in your custody record. Keep the original package intact and work from copies. Share evidence files rather than the application's private data directory, which also contains account sessions and signing secrets. For transfer, an export can be put into a password-protected AES-256 ZIP. The password only protects confidentiality and is not stored; the recipient extracts the archive and verifies the signed export inside, which is unchanged. pages.description: Run a witness with its own key and bot, publish signed checkpoints to a channel and check exports against it.
pages.keywords: witness bot channel checkpoint tgw1 verify continuity
pages.text: Настройка бота и прокси на русском . A collector signs its own journal, so whoever controls the collector and its key could in principle rewrite or truncate the journal and sign it again. A witness makes that detectable. It is a separate process — another container, or better a server someone else runs — that every few minutes fetches the collector's signed journal head, signs what it saw with its own key, keeps it in its own journal and posts it to a Telegram channel. Diagram as text Collector → Witness (signed checkpoint: record count + head hash) Witness → Witness journal, own key Witness → Telegram channel (signed post via its own bot) Evidence ZIP → verify.py Witness journal, own key → verify.py Telegram channel → verify.py (Telegram Desktop export or t.me/s page) What the witness gets, and what it does not # The witness has The witness never has A read-only witness token for one workspace The collector's Telegram session or API credentials Its own Ed25519 key and journal The collector's vault, signing key or panel token Its own Telegram bot token Message content: the head is a record count and a hash The token is created on the panel's Witness page, shown once and stored only as a SHA-256. It opens exactly one endpoint, GET /api/witness/head , which returns a freshly signed checkpoint plus signed content-free collection counters and operational health. It cannot open the panel, read message content or change settings, and the panel token is not accepted there. Revoke a token on the same page. The collector records when a new witness key starts checking ( witness.seen ) and shows the last check per token; a witness that has not checked within 2.5 intervals is marked overdue. New witnesses send a random challenge on each poll; the capture statement echoes it under the collector signature. Counters are bound to the exact checkpoint and are included in signed witness posts. Legacy heads remain accepted by the standalone witness. Journal growth alone is never counted as a new message. What it checks and records # Every interval (10 minutes by default) the witness: fetches the head itself (the collector cannot push or skip it); verifies the collector's signature, the pinned collector key ( --collector-fingerprint , or the first key seen), a nondecreasing count and an unchanged head at an unchanged count; appends a signed record to its own journal: witness.anchor with status ok , key_changed , rollback (fewer records than before), fork (same length, different head) or invalid (the answer failed verification), or witness.no_response when the collector did not answer; posts the result to the channel, signed, including "no answer" while the witness is running and can reach the Bot API. The post ID is recorded ( witness.posted ), a failed post too ( witness.post_failed ). A post looks like this; the last line carries the signed statement: TgWitness witness #42 · journal head Collector 3fa9c2d1e0b4a7f6: 18234 records Head 9b1f…c07e 2026-10-28T19:40:00.123+00:00 TGW1.eyJhdCI6…<statement>.<signature> Run a witness # You need a Telegram bot (create one with @BotFather), a channel where that bot is an administrator, and the collector's address reachable from the witness — over HTTPS outside a private network (see the HTTPS profile in deployment ). Open Extras → A bot in your channel → Set up a bot in the panel. Three steps cover read-only access, your channel and interval, then launching the witness. Publication policy, optional HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy and custom Bot API address are under Advanced settings . The form downloads witness.json with this workspace's collector key pinned. Download the newly created read-only token with Save access file as witness-token.txt ; place it and a bot-token.txt created on the witness host beside that JSON. The collector never receives the bot token. Downloading does not start a service or publish a message. No hosted project witness is implicitly enrolled. python -m tgwitness.witness run --config witness.j

pages.title: Reference · Timestamps
pages.description: RFC 3161 timestamps for signed checkpoints: what is sent to the authority and how a response is verified.
pages.keywords: rfc 3161 tsa timestamp authority nonce checkpoint
pages.text: TgWitness prepares RFC 3161 requests and verifies timestamp authority (TSA) responses. This manual procedure neither selects a TSA nor submits data; evidence mode does both on a schedule ( evidence format ). A prepared request is not yet a timestamp proof . What the proof binds # Diagram as text Account observations → SHA-256 chain and Ed25519 signatures SHA-256 chain and Ed25519 signatures → Signed checkpoint Signed checkpoint → Exact-byte hash and random nonce Exact-byte hash and random nonce → RFC 3161 request RFC 3161 request → Independent TSA Independent TSA → Signed TSA response Signed checkpoint → Verify data, nonce and explicit CA trust Signed TSA response → Verify data, nonce and explicit CA trust The collector signature binds records to its key. A trusted TSA response can establish that a particular checkpoint existed by the TSA's stated time. The checkpoint can then bind the journal prefix. This does not establish the time of each Telegram action or the truth of the captured content. Procedure # Retain the collector key fingerprint through a separate trusted channel. A key supplied only by the examined ZIP is insufficient to identify the collector. In Exports → Prepare timestamp request , download the selected workspace's request ZIP. Extract checkpoint.json , timestamp.tsq , SHA256SUMS and README.txt . Do not change the checkpoint bytes. Choose a TSA appropriate to the investigation. Submit timestamp.tsq using its documented method, with application/timestamp-query for an HTTP service. Save the original binary reply as timestamp.tsr , the endpoint, retrieval time and request outcome. The request contains a hash and nonce rather than messages; network metadata still reveals the request. Obtain the trusted root certificate independently of the reply, plus any intermediates required. A certificate in the reply does not become trusted merely because it is included there. From a trusted TgWitness installation, verify: python -m tgwitness.anchor verify --checkpoint checkpoint.json --request timestamp.tsq --response timestamp.tsr --ca trusted-tsa-root.pem Add --intermediates tsa-intermediates.pem or --openssl /path/to/openssl if needed. OpenSSL must support ts . On Windows the verifier also searches the standard Git installation. OpenSSL 3.5.9 was tested locally with a synthetic CA/TSA. Export a signed journal ZIP after the checkpoint so it includes that prefix. Verify using the independently known fingerprint: python tgwitness/verify.py evidence.zip --fingerprint TRUSTED_SHA256 --checkpoint checkpoint.json Preserve the ZIP, checkpoint, request, reply, certificate chain, verification results and handoff record outside the collector. Repeat verification at receipt. To prepare a request from a saved checkpoint: python -m tgwitness.anchor prepare checkpoint.json --out timestamp-request.zip Preparation canonicalizes JSON and includes the matching checkpoint in the archive. Use the checkpoint bytes from that archive for TSA verification, even if the input file had different whitespace. Verification boundaries # Check Current behavior Data SHA-256 of the exact checkpoint bytes must match the response Request With --request , the original query and nonce are verified TSA signature OpenSSL verifies the signature and chain to the explicit CA Collector signature Separately verified by the journal verifier with a pinned key Revocation No automatic OCSP/CRL retrieval Long-term validity No archival validation after certificate expiry Scheduled submission Evidence mode, off by default --request is technically optional, but omitting it prevents verification of the original nonce. For this full procedure, the result's request_checked must be true. Certificate verification follows the installed OpenSSL's rules and verification time. Long-term preservation needs a separate certificate/revocation evidence policy. A valid cryptographic signature is not automatically a qualified timestamp or a legal admissibility determination. pages.title: Reference · Security and data handling
pages.description: Threat model, access model, secrets at rest, network exposure, session imports and how to report a vulnerability.
pages.keywords: security threat model token vault fernet encryption report vulnerability
pages.text: TgWitness runs on your own computer or server. Account connections, public proxy-list upkeep and optional external services have explicit routing policies. Notifications, timestamps, off-site copies and a witness are separately configured. This page lists what is protected, how, and what is left to the operator. Area In short Access Administrator key plus scoped access to accounts/chats, seven permissions and revocable sessions; localhost by default Secrets at rest Session, API pair, signing key and proxy settings are encrypted with Fernet Messages and media Stored unencrypted: use disk encryption and strict permissions Integrity SHA-256 hash chain and an Ed25519 signature on every record Not covered A machine administrator, a leaked panel token, completeness of capture For vulnerability reports, see the security policy . Access model # The main panel token grants full control. Other people can receive their own scoped access : chosen workspaces and chats, permissions, expiry, IP restrictions, sign-in limits and revocable sessions. A chat-limited access cannot perform whole-workspace operations even if their permission is ticked. Workspaces share a process and do not isolate data from the host administrator. The panel listens on localhost by default. Browser sign-in exchanges an access token for a session credential; the browser sends it as a bearer token. It is kept in sessionStorage rather than an authentication cookie. Lock/sign-out clears the browser session. Closing a browser or ending a session does not stop collection. Issued tokens and session credentials are kept as hashes in the encrypted vault. Revocation ends the associated sessions; permission changes affect subsequent requests. Downloaded files cannot be recalled. The administrator can limit their own browser sessions too, but scripts using the main panel token directly retain full access and bypass those browser-session limits. Failed authentication is rate-limited by client address. IP restrictions use the address seen by the application; check reverse-proxy behavior before relying on it. Witness credentials remain separate read-only checkpoint/health credentials. Demo access # /api/demo-access is a deliberately unauthenticated bootstrap for an explicitly started, isolated synthetic demo. It issues a separate process-lifetime capability, never the real panel token or a TGWITNESS_TOKEN override. Issuance and use require a loopback peer and Host, no forwarded headers, and no cross-origin request. Additional workspaces or an authorized session disable this path. Live workspaces never issue the capability. The demo cannot connect accounts or change collection settings. Panel content and exports # The panel uses no external fonts, analytics, CDN resources, or embedded remote media. Telegram-sourced text is inserted as text, not HTML. Downloaded attachments are served as binary attachments. JSONL exports preserve original strings; HTML escapes them; CSV cells that could become formulas are prefixed with an apostrophe. Exports exclude authentication and signing secrets, but deliberately contain collected source metadata, identifiers, and possibly personal or sensitive content. Telegram access hashes and file references can occur in raw source metadata. Secrets at rest # Telegram API credentials, StringSession, and the Ed25519 private key are encrypted using Fernet. By default its key is stored in the same protected data directory. This reduces accidental plaintext exposure; it is not protection against an attacker who can read the whole directory. Message content and media are not encrypted by TgWitness. Use disk encryption and restrictive OS permissions. Unix private key files are created with mode 0600; newly created data directories use mode 0700. Existing directory permissions are not changed. Windows inherits directory ACLs: restrict them to the service account and authorized administrators. External master key # For a new data directory, TGWITNESS_VAULT_KEY_FILE

pages.text: One Python process hosts the FastAPI panel and any number of isolated workspaces, each with a Telethon user-account client. SQLite holds an append-only signed event journal and mutable operational settings. An encrypted vault holds API credentials, the StringSession, and signing key. The frontend is plain bundled HTML/CSS/JavaScript: no Node build, CDNs, or runtime frontend downloads are needed. Live collection is gated by the active client identity, explicit running state, enabled sources or the observation scope (folder or whole-account modes add a new chat as a source on its first update), and event policy. Rejected and superseded clients cannot contribute live updates. Raw reactions and membership updates preserve visibility limits. Incoming message content and its durable media job are committed together. Jobs preserve the original TL descriptor and bind its hash to the signed message observation. Sender/editor/deleter semantics are separated. Each workspace accepts one account and has its own directory and signing identity. The main workspace remains at the root for compatibility; additional workspaces live in profiles/<id>/. One bearer token controls the whole installation; workspaces are not separate authorization tenants. Process locks protect
